title: Collector UI must conform to a shared design system profile and remain semantically accessible
trigger: Applies to collector-family Clanks that present an operator dashboard or local web UI for monitoring, scheduling, or reviewing automated collection. A Clank with no operator-facing web surface is N/A. Does not automatically apply to non-collector Clanks (CTW, KTW, Semiconductor) unless independently adopted.
requirement: A collector-family Clank that presents an operator dashboard MUST conform to a declared Collector UI Design System profile: it MUST report the design-system version it conforms to, MUST render every status with a text label (colour is supplementary), MUST display the full Clank identity (never a generic abbreviation alone), MUST provide meaningful empty states that explain what the absence means, MUST use consistent navigation grammar for equivalent concepts across the collector family, MUST NOT ship the Phase-0 scaffold as a finished operator UI, bare 'Empty' placeholders, generic-only 'Clank' branding, or colour-only status conveyance, and MUST present a desktop-first layout usable at 1080p and 1440p operator workstations. Where GUI-triggered collection is part of the product's intended operator workflow: GUI load MUST remain side-effect free, collection MUST require explicit operator intent, collection MUST use the canonical execution/locking/state path, and the resulting run state MUST be inspectable. A read-only GUI is acceptable where read-only operation is intentional and documented; a read-only Phase-0 scaffold MUST NOT masquerade as a finished interactive operator UI when the intended workflow requires collection controls. Domain-specific visual adaptations beyond the shared token set are permitted where they preserve family recognisability, shell/hierarchy, navigation grammar, typography hierarchy, component semantics, status semantics, density/layout quality, accessibility, and operator workflow clarity.
rationale: The six collector Clanks form one internal product suite with six domain personalities. Before the visual redesign, each dashboard was an independently built Phase-0 scaffold with generic branding, bare empty states, collapsed run status, inconsistent health/delivery visual vocabulary, and no shared visual recognisability. The current implementation (a byte-identical collector_ui.py design system module with per-Clank accent-only overrides) eliminates those problems without introducing a runtime dependency; however, the normative contract is about design conformance, not implementation format. Future implementations may use Jinja templates, SPA components, generated assets, build-time packages, or other architectures, provided the declared design-system profile is satisfied.
forbidden: Rendering status using colour alone without a text label
Displaying a generic 'Clank' brand name without the full Clank product identity
Shipping bare 'Empty' placeholder text in place of a meaningful empty state explanation
Shipping the Phase-0 scaffold as a finished operator UI when the intended workflow requires collection controls
Using a content width or layout that leaves giant dead-space on a 1080p or 1440p operator desktop
Collapsing pipeline stages the backend already distinguishes into a single undifferentiated status
Triggering collection as a side effect of GUI load, page GET, or startup
Allowing a read-only scaffold to present itself as a finished interactive operator UI
acceptance: The Clank declares which Collector UI design system profile and version it conforms to
Every rendered status badge carries its label as visible text; colour is supplementary
The full Clank product name is visible in the dashboard header
Empty states explain what the absence means, not just 'Empty'

Domain-specific visual adaptations preserve family recognisability, shell/hierarchy, navigation grammar, typography hierarchy, component semantics, status semantics, density/layout quality, accessibility, and operator workflow clarity
No template or rendered output contains the prohibited Phase-0 scaffold labels or bare 'Empty' text
The layout is usable and information-dense at 1080p and 1440p viewport widths
GUI load does not trigger collection as a side effect
Where GUI-triggered collection exists, it requires explicit operator intent and uses the canonical execution/locking/state path, with results inspectable

evidence.summary: Six collector Clanks implemented a shared collector_ui.py design system with per-Clank accent-only overrides, proven by SHA-256 hash equality across all six copies. This is the current reference implementation, not the only permitted implementation architecture.
Browser-first acceptance record demonstrating that semantic/static checks alone cannot prove visual quality; operator visual inspection remains a required evidence type.
Compatibility refusal must remain fail-closed but surface actionable operator context, not raw compatibility tracebacks.

notes: PROPOSED — not yet ratified. This standard formalises the visual/operator design system contract for the collector-family Clanks. It is deliberately separate from the frozen semantic UI standards (STD-UI-COM-001..012, STD-UI-NEWS-001/002, STD-UI-SKU-001), which govern semantic behaviour, not visual presentation. Implementation detail (exact CSS selectors, exact pixel values beyond the token scale, hover/transition effects, specific component helper names, whether the design system ships as a Python constant vs CSS file vs SPA components vs build-time package) is NOT normative. The design-system profile/version identifier is normative (conforming implementations MUST declare which profile they target); how that profile is satisfied (Python constant, Jinja, SPA, generated CSS) is implementation detail. The current reference implementation is a byte-identical Python module with per-Clank accent-only overrides; that is evidence for the six current implementations, not a constraint on future architectures. Domain-specific visual adaptations are permitted where they preserve family recognisability, shell/hierarchy, navigation grammar, typography hierarchy, component semantics, status semantics, density/layout quality, accessibility, and operator workflow clarity.
